source.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a controlled toy-network result about recovery and geometry of planted features, using a compressed autoencoder and direction matching; it does not state that it reproduces the original method.
record.gate_note: Figure 13 reports results from the paper's own Elhage-style toy-network experiment. The paper's generic descriptions of other experiments and its transformer activation results do not directly test the listed superposition versions. The moderate-sparsity regime is named but its outcome is not described.
record.test_reason: This is a sparse-PCA (FACET) methods paper. Its one superposition-related result, Figure 13, uses an Elhage-style toy autoencoder (n=12 features, d=6) as a testbed for comparing recovery by FACET, PCA and a third method. The toy's geometry is mentioned only qualitatively, in a caption, to explain the recovery ceilings. There are no numbers, no sweep analysis and no claim about superposition itself. The GPT-2, ViT and SAE panels report the method's reconstruction, sparsity and coherence, not whether LLMs show superposition or whether SAE features are canonical.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarises the Figure 13 caption: antipodal pairs at low density with FACET exact on unique directions, and 12 distinct directions in the dense regime that an m=d basis cannot match. The paper's overall conclusion, however, is about the method. FACET is a corrected block sparse-PCA estimator with convergence and identification guarantees, matching PCA reconstruction while being sparser and more interpretable. It also avoids the roughly 8-point R² cost of a matched-width tied SAE.
record.recipe_differences: The reported setup is an Elhage-style compressed autoencoder trained with importance-weighted reconstruction, evaluated using Hungarian direction matching and compared with PCA and FACET; further method details are not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: The described geometry differs between the very-sparse and dense regimes; the moderate-regime outcome is not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy autoencoder (n=12, d=6), FACET recovers each unique planted direction at very high sparsity, while PCA mixes them under importance decay. Hungarian matching is used because a lenient max-cos metric is inflated by antipodal collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The choice of decomposition method and matching metric affects measured recovery of superposed toy features; antipodal pairs cap recoverable unique directions at d.

record.problems: Figure 13 gives qualitative outcomes but no numerical matching scores, uncertainty, or replication count for this experiment. The moderate-sparsity outcome is not described.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant result rows were left out. The moderate regime in Figure 13 has no stated outcome; Sections 8.2 and 8.3 provide generic descriptions rather than additional results testing these versions.

untested.parts: Not tested as a claim. The paper gives no quantified geometry, interference measure or phase transition. The moderate-sparsity outcome is not reported.
Whole version untested. The GPT-2 panels evaluate FACET against PCA and an SAE, not feature spread or SAE recovery as evidence of superposition.
Whole version untested. The SAE comparison concerns reconstruction cost at matched width, not the completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The toy-model geometry statement (pair-antipodal at low density) is consistent with the original Toy Models paper rather than contrary to it. It is an incidental, unquantified caption remark, so I give no verdict. Section 8.2 announces a toy superposition network and a small transformer, but Figure 13 is the only reported result. Single author, preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment does not establish a general sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry across settings, quantify interference, or test the corresponding claim in LLMs. The moderate-sparsity outcome is not stated.
The experiment does not test whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while less important ones share capacity.
No result tests whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The LLM experiments do not test whether features spread across neurons or whether an SAE recovers such features.
The SAE comparison does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper does not compare one-dimensional feature representations with multidimensional ones.

conditions.value: very sparse, approximately 1 feature active per sample

rows.measure: Hungarian-matched direction recovery and distinct planted directions
rows.value: Low-density features form pair-antipodal arrangements (u=d=6); FACET recovers every unique direction exactly.
rows.note: The reported antipodal pairs share a direction up to sign, rather than forming a set of nearly orthogonal directions. The paper says all three methods are bounded by the same unique-direction budget in this regime.
rows.check: This is mainly a method-performance row (FACET recovers each unique direction), so it should not link to V1. The 'reversed' state is also wrong. Pair-antipodal arrangements of 12 features in 6 dimensions are a regular superposition geometry described in the original Toy Models paper, not evidence against near-orthogonal storage. The caption gives no numbers.
